decision: Made incFixLoop/resetFixLoop assigns a no-op when the counter is untracked (undefined) in context, instead of the plan's plain nullish-base increment.
alternatives: custom serializeState in the graph test
reasoning: getAdjacencyMap serializes the full snapshot (value+context) via JSON.stringify, so a context-mutating assign with a nullish base makes structural exploration mint an ever-growing counter and diverge into an infinite state space (the graph test hung). Editing the graph test's serializeState was disallowed (ac-16: passes unchanged). No-op-when-untracked keeps the machine's default {} context invariant during exploration (finite, 169 rows) while the live write path always seeds counters via LucaState schema defaults, so production increments/resets normally; parity (value/reason only) is unaffected.
risk: If a future caller ever drives the machine with a counter absent from context but expecting an increment, the assign silently no-ops. Mitigated: the LucaState schema defaults every counter to 0, so the write path never passes undefined.
reviewHint: Confirm the no-op-when-untracked invariant is acceptable vs. the plan's plain nullish increment; it is the load-bearing reason the graph test terminates.
